tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch. When the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and boots one that is off, so do not boot a simulator yourself. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app. Build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch. When the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and boots one that is off, so do not boot a simulator yourself. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app. Build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user. Call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and it boots one that is off and returns while that one is still starting up. Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches: the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition: 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'set_posture' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'state': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'posture' reports the state, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the state and angle with 'posture'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'set_posture' and take a 'screenshot'; if the open screen shows the app with black bars and the target sets UIRequiresFullScreen, tell the user the key is the likely cause and keep it unless they ask; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag: left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator this session already uses, else a booted one no other session is using, else the first booted one. If none is booted, 'attach' boots the only one the user already allowed, and 'launch' does so or asks for 'attach' first; if there is not exactly one, name one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key' and the volume buttons: how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

angle.description: For 'set_posture' with state 'half_open': the hinge angle in degrees, 1 to 179 (0 is shut, 180 flat); default 130.

Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

"""Web app: can herding explain market crashes?

Run on this computer:  streamlit run app.py   (then open http://localhost:8501)

Pages live in web/ (one file each); web/common.py holds the shared colors, spacing and cached data.
The pages only draw. Every number comes from herding/explore.py (tested in tests/test_explore.py),
which runs the model in herding/model.py (docs/SPEC.md).
"""
import importlib
import os

import streamlit as st

# The site's own modules, each after the ones it imports. Streamlit reruns app.py and the pages on
# every visit, but keeps imported modules in memory: after a push the live server kept the old
# herding/explore.py and web/common.py and crashed ("setup() takes 0 positional arguments",
# "no attribute KIRMAN_PASS", Nov 2026) until someone rebooted it by hand.
SITE_MODULES = ["herding.checks", "herding.stats", "herding.model", "herding.market_data",
                "herding.calibrate", "herding.experiments", "herding.politics", "herding.factors",
                "herding.kirman", "herding.explore", "web.common"]


def _loaded_at(m):
    """When this copy of module m was loaded. After a reload here it is recorded in m._site_mtime.
    Before that (a module imported before this check ran, like on the live server the first time):
    the time of its compiled .pyc file, which Python writes or checks when it imports the module,
    so a source file newer than its .pyc changed after the module was loaded."""
    if hasattr(m, "_site_mtime"):
        return m._site_mtime
    cached = getattr(m, "__cached__", None)
    return os.path.getmtime(cached) if cached and os.path.exists(cached) else os.path.getmtime(m.__file__)


def reload_if_changed(names=SITE_MODULES):
    """Reload all the site's modules, in order, when any of their files changed since it was loaded.
    Returns the names reloaded (empty when nothing changed)."""
    mods = [importlib.import_module(n) for n in names]
    if not any(os.path.getmtime(m.__file__) > _loaded_at(m) for m in mods):
        for m in mods:
            m._site_mtime = _loaded_at(m)
        return []
    for n in names:               # all of them, in order, so nobody keeps a reference to an old copy
        m = importlib.reload(importlib.import_module(n))
        m._site_mtime = os.path.getmtime(m.__file__)
    return list(names)


# The page list and the top navigation go out first, before the site's modules are imported (about
# half a second on a fresh server: pandas, numba, the model), so the navigation bar can show while
# the rest loads. TEST_PROGRAM must equal web.common.TEST_PROGRAM (tests/test_web_style.py checks).
TEST_PROGRAM = "Test program"
st.set_page_config(page_title="Herding and market crashes", page_icon="📉", layout="wide",
                   initial_sidebar_state="auto")   # open on wide screens; "expanded" covered the page on phones
PAGES = [
    st.Page("web/page_guide.py", title="Start here", icon=":material/home:", default=True),
    st.Page("web/page_story.py", title="Story", icon=":material/auto_stories:"),
    st.Page("web/page_explore.py", title=TEST_PROGRAM, icon=":material/candlestick_chart:"),
    st.Page("web/page_compare.py", title="Compare", icon=":material/scatter_plot:"),
    st.Page("web/page_checks.py", title="Checks", icon=":material/fact_check:"),
    st.Page("web/page_findings.py", title="Findings", icon=":material/photo_library:"),
]
nav = st.navigation(PAGES, position="top")

reload_if_changed()
from web import common  # noqa: E402  (after the reload, so this is the current copy)

# every page's address, so the light/dark button can set the mode for pages not opened yet, and the
# navigation numbers each page by its address. After st.navigation: a page only gets its url_path
# when navigation registers it (reading it first crashed the live site on a fresh start, Nov 2026)
common.setup(["/" + (pg.url_path or "") for pg in PAGES], nav.title)
nav.run()

For comparison, the Dow's real gap since 1896 is " 719 "about +3.5% a year, which is about what luck alone gives (turn on President's party on " 720 "the Price chart).") 721 sp_days = c.default_run()["days"] 722 # full width with a short label: in half the narrow panel, "19,329 (as long as the S&P 500 723 # record)" was cut to "19,329 (as lo" 724 st.selectbox("Days", [5000, 10000, sp_days], key="in_days", 725 format_func=lambda d: f"{d:,}" + (" (S&P 500 length)" if d == sp_days else ""), 726 help=f"How many trading days to simulate. {sp_days:,} is as long as the S&P 500's " 727 f"record since 1950.") 728 st.number_input("Seed", 0, 10_000, key="in_seed", help="Which random history.") 729 if st.button("Run model", type="primary", width="stretch"): 730 new = {"a1": float(ss.in_a1), "a2": float(ss.in_a2), "v1": float(ss.in_v1), 731 "days": int(ss.in_days), "seed": int(ss.in_seed), "party": float(ss.in_party)} 732 with st.spinner("Running..."): 733 res = c.run_mixes(**new) 734 _log_run(new, res) 735 ss.run = new 736 st.rerun() 737 if _controls_changed(): 738 st.markdown("

"""Test program (was "Workspace"): one market next to the model. top the market picker: a tab per kind of market (Indexes, Stocks, Commodities), a button per saved market, and a box for any ticker Yahoo Finance knows (fetched live) header the market's name, last price and day change, and the Live prices switch left column range numbers and a chart with ranges 1D-All and five views (a fragment: changing the view or range reruns only the chart) right column the model: three sliders, days and seed, Run model with a line saying what ran, and the tail exponent against herding strength with every run you make. On a phone the columns stack, so the model comes right after the chart below tables: model vs market, big days, and the run log sidebar model presets that fill in the sliders """ import time from datetime import datetime import numpy as np import pandas as pd import plotly.graph_objects as go import streamlit as st from plotly.subplots import make_subplots from herding import explore as ex from web import common as c VIEWS = ["Price", "Tail", "Histogram", "Bursts", "Memory"] # one sentence under each chart for first-time visitors: what it shows and what to look for HINTS = { "Price": "The price over the range you picked. Triangles mark days that moved more than 4 standard " "deviations; a bell curve says those should almost never happen. The lower panel shows how far " "the price sits below its last high.", "Tail": "How often big days happen. Read left to right: the further a line stays up, the more often " "big moves happen. The dotted bell curve drops off fast; look for the line that follows this market best.", "Histogram": "How common each size of daily move is. Compared with the dotted bell curve, real markets have " "more quiet days in the middle and more extreme days at the edges.", "Bursts": "Each day's move, measured in standard deviations. Notice that wild days come in clusters, both in " "the real market (top) and in the herding model (bottom, when its history did not run away).", "Memory": "Does a big move today mean big moves later? Above 0 means yes. Real markets stay above 0 for " "months; the bell-curve model drops to 0 at once.", } PRESETS = {"S&P 500 fit": None, "Strong herding": 1.6, "Weak herding": 0.6, "No herding": 0.0} SAVED_BY_SYMBOL = {v: k for k, v in ex.YAHOO.items()} # ^GSPC -> S&P 500, GC=F -> Gold, ... NO_INTRADAY_NOTE = "Prices within the day need Live prices on, so this shows the last daily closes." YAHOO_DOWN_NOTE = "Yahoo Finance isn't answering, so this shows the saved daily closes." FAIL_MEMORY = 300 # seconds a failed Yahoo fetch is remembered, so every rerun doesn't ask again def _init(): ss = st.session_state ss.setdefault("asset", ("saved", "S&P 500")) ss.setdefault("ticker_error", "") ss.setdefault("ticker_error_for", None) # the market on screen when the error was made ss.setdefault("run", c.default_run()) ss.setdefault("log", []) # the tab follows the market on screen: a saved market's own tab; a live ticker keeps the tab open ss.setdefault("group", ex.market_group(ss.asset[1]) or "Indexes") # _load fell back to the S&P 500 after a run had drawn the ticker box: clear it now, before the # box is drawn (a widget's value can't be changed after it is drawn in the same run) if ss.pop("_fallback_done", False): ss.ticker_box = "" ss.group = "Indexes" if "party" not in ss.run: # a session from before the party drift existed ss.run = dict(ss.run, party=0.0) for k in ("a1", "a2", "v1", "days", "seed", "party"): ss.setdefault(f"in_{k}", ss.run[k]) # the preset picked is the one the controls match now, or none: a radio that kept showing # "S&P 500 fit" after a slider moved could not be clicked again to restore the fit ss.preset = _matching_preset() def _matching_preset(): ss = st.session_state p, _ = c.fitted() for name, a1 in PRESETS.items(): want = {"in_a1": float(p["a1"]) if a1 is None else a1, "in_a2": float(p["a2"]), "in_v1": float(p["v1"]), "in_party": 0.0} if all(abs(float(ss[k]) - v) < 1e-9 for k, v in want.items()): return name return None def _pick_market(key): """A market button was clicked. Clicking the picked one again would unpick it: keep it picked. Either way the visitor chose a market, so an old ticker error and the typed text are cleared (left in the box, typing the same ticker again changed nothing, so nothing happened).""" ss = st.session_state v = ss[key] if v is None: ss[key] = ss.asset[1] else: ss.asset = ("saved", v) ss.ticker_error = "" ss.ticker_box = "" ss.typed_symbol = None def _fetch(): """The ticker box: a saved market's ticker or Yahoo symbol opens the saved market (and its tab); anything else is fetched live from Yahoo and keeps the tab open. On success the box is emptied, so typing the same ticker again later works; on an error the text stays, to be corrected.""" ss = st.session_state if not ss.ticker_box.strip(): # emptying the box is not an error: keep the market ss.ticker_error = "" return try: t = ex.clean_ticker(ss.ticker_box) if t in ex.market_data.stock_tickers(): ss.asset = ("saved", t) elif t in SAVED_BY_SYMBOL: # ^GSPC, GC=F, ...: the saved market with that symbol ss.asset = ("saved", SAVED_BY_SYMBOL[t]) else: c.live_asset(t) ss.asset = ("live", t) ss.ticker_error = "" ss.ticker_box = "" ss.typed_symbol = t if ss.asset[0] == "saved": ss.group = ex.market_group(ss.asset[1]) _forget_failure(("daily", t)) except ConnectionError: ss.ticker_error = ex.YAHOO_DOWN except ValueError as e: msg = str(e) # (str.capitalize would lower-case the ticker) ss.ticker_error = msg[:1].upper() + msg[1:] ss.ticker_error_for = ss.asset def _failed_recently(key, now=None): """True if fetching `key` from Yahoo failed less than FAIL_MEMORY seconds ago (this visitor).""" t = st.session_state.get("live_failed", {}).get(key) return t is not None and (time.time() if now is None else now) - t < FAIL_MEMORY def _remember_failure(key): st.session_state.setdefault("live_failed", {})[key] = time.time() def _forget_failure(key): st.session_state.get("live_failed", {}).pop(key, None) def _preset(): p, _ = c.fitted() a1 = PRESETS[st.session_state.preset] st.session_state.in_a1 = float(p["a1"]) if a1 is None else a1 st.session_state.in_a2, st.session_state.in_v1 = float(p["a2"]), float(p["v1"]) st.session_state.in_party = 0.0 # a preset is the fit itself: no party drift GROUPS = {"Indexes": "A whole market in one number: the S&P 500 is 500 large US companies " "(an index fund buys all of them).", "Stocks": "Single companies: 20 large US stocks that rise and fall about 1% when the market " "moves 1% (market beta 0.9–1.1).", "Commodities": "Raw materials traded worldwide: oil, gold and copper. (Brent oil's saved and live " "prices come from two sources, spot and futures, and can differ: usually by 1–2%, " "but by up to 25% in 2026.)"} def _picker(): """The market picker at the top of the page: a tab per kind of market, a button per market, and a box for any ticker.""" ss = st.session_state _, name = ss.asset with st.container(key="picker", border=True): left, right = st.columns([3, 1.3], gap="medium") with left: # no default: the tab is seeded in session state (_init) and set by _fetch, and a widget # given both a default and a session-state value makes Streamlit warn group = c.pick_one("Pick a market", list(GROUPS), None, "group", format_func=lambda g: f"{g} ({len(ex.catalog()[g])})") st.markdown(f"

{GROUPS[group]}

", unsafe_allow_html=True) names = ex.catalog()[group] key = f"pick_{group}_{name}" # a new key when the market changes: the right button lit if key not in ss: # seeded, not a default: same reason as the tab ss[key] = name if name in names else None st.pills("Markets", names, key=key, format_func=ex.display_name, on_change=_pick_market, args=(key,), label_visibility="collapsed") with right: st.text_input("Or type any ticker", key="ticker_box", placeholder="e.g. NVDA, then Enter", max_chars=12, on_change=_fetch, help="Any symbol Yahoo Finance knows: a stock, a fund like SPY, " "or crypto like BTC-USD. Needs the internet.\n\n" "Won't work: companies listed for 4 years or less; prices " "that barely move (stablecoins, pegged currencies); " "measurements rather than prices (volatility indexes like " "^VIX, interest rates like ^TNX); unknown or delisted " "tickers.") # shown only while the same market is on screen: picking another one makes the error stale if ss.ticker_error and ss.ticker_error_for == ss.asset: st.error(ss.ticker_error) def _sidebar(): with st.sidebar: st.radio("Model presets", list(PRESETS), index=None, key="preset", on_change=_preset, captions=["the fitted settings", "a1 = 1.6", "a1 = 0.6, often runs away", "a1 = 0, chartists don't copy"]) st.caption("A preset fills in the controls. Press Run model to use it.") def _load(live): ss = st.session_state source, name = ss.asset if source == "live": # the cached prices of a typed ticker last 24 hours (or until Clear cache); fetching them # again can fail while the visitor still has that ticker open, which used to replace the # whole page with a red ConnectionError (WS-23). Fall back to the S&P 500 and say why. try: return (*c.live_asset(name), "live", name) except (ConnectionError, ValueError): ss.asset = ("saved", "S&P 500") ss.ticker_error = (f"Live prices for {name} aren't available right now. Showing the S&P 500. " f"Type {name} again in a minute, or pick a market above.") ss.ticker_error_for = ss.asset ss.typed_symbol = None ss._fallback_done = True # next run: empty the ticker box, Indexes tab st.toast(ss.ticker_error) return (*c.saved_asset("S&P 500"), "saved", "S&P 500") # not live again: Yahoo just failed if live: symbol = ex.yahoo_symbol(name) if not _failed_recently(("daily", symbol)): # Yahoo just failed: don't ask on every click try: return (*c.live_asset(symbol), "live", name) except (ConnectionError, ValueError): _remember_failure(("daily", symbol)) st.toast(f"Live prices for {name} aren't available right now, so this shows the saved data.") return (*c.saved_asset(name), "saved", name) def _log_ticks(lo, hi): """(values, labels) for a log price axis from lo to hi: powers of ten read 1, 10, 100, 1,000 (plotly's own labels put small "2" and "5" between them). When fewer than 3 powers of ten fall in the range, 2 and 5 times them are added, written out in full; None when the range is inside one step (plotly's own labels are fine there).""" lo, hi = float(lo), float(hi) if not (0 < lo <= hi and np.isfinite(hi)): raise ValueError(f"need 0 < lo <= hi, got {lo}, {hi}") ks = range(int(np.floor(np.log10(lo))), int(np.ceil(np.log10(hi))) + 1) vals = [10.0 ** k for k in ks if lo <= 10.0 ** k <= hi] if len(vals) < 3: vals = [m * 10.0 ** k for k in ks for m in (1, 2, 5) if lo <= m * 10.0 ** k <= hi] if len(vals) < 2: return None labels = [f"{v:,.0f}" if v >= 1 else np.format_float_positional(v, precision=12, trim="-") for v in vals] return vals, labels def _price_chart(name, cl, r, daily_range, show_big, show_dd, log, intraday, hours=None, party=False): """The price (in the market's own color: up/down colors only go with an arrow), big days as triangles, and the drawdown below. A short range of daily closes (1D or 7D without prices within the day) is drawn with a dot at each close and one date per day, not hours.""" rows = 2 if show_dd else 1 fig = make_subplots(rows=rows, cols=1, shared_xaxes=True, vertical_spacing=0.05, row_heights=[0.74, 0.26] if show_dd else [1]) x, y = c.thin(cl.index, cl.values) fmt = "%b %d %H:%M" if intraday else "%b %d, %Y" few_days = not intraday and len(cl) <= 10 fig.add_scatter(x=x, y=y, mode="lines+markers" if few_days else "lines", name=name, line=dict(color=c.REAL, width=1.8), hovertemplate=f"%{{x|{fmt}}}
%{{y:,.{ex.price_decimals(cl.min())}f}}", row=1, col=1) if show_big and not intraday: big = ex.big_day_list(r, within=ex.moves_in_range(r, daily_range)) # not the move into the first day for up, sym, col in ((True, "triangle-up", c.UP), (False, "triangle-down", c.DOWN)): b = big[(big["move"] > 0) == up] fig.add_scatter(x=b.index, y=daily_range[b.index].values, mode="markers", name=f"Big {'rise' if up else 'fall'} (> 4 sd)", marker=dict(symbol=sym, size=10, color=col, line=dict(color=c.BG, width=1)), customdata=np.c_[b["move"], b["sd"]], hovertemplate="%{x|%b %d, %Y}
%{customdata[0]:+.1%} (%{customdata[1]:+.1f} sd)", row=1, col=1) if show_dd: dd = ex.drawdown_series(cl) x, y = c.thin(dd.index, dd.values) fig.add_scatter(x=x, y=y, mode="lines", name="▼ Drawdown", fill="tozeroy", # loss color with its arrow line=dict(color=c.DOWN, width=1), fillcolor=c.DOWN_FILL, hovertemplate=f"%{{x|{fmt}}}
%{{y:.1%}} below the high", row=2, col=1) if party and not intraday: _shade_parties(fig, cl.index) c.style(fig, height=470) fig.update_yaxes(type="log" if log else "-", title="Price", row=1, col=1) ticks = _log_ticks(cl.min(), cl.max()) if log else None if ticks: fig.update_yaxes(tickvals=ticks[0], ticktext=ticks[1], row=1, col=1) if show_dd: # a range that never fell is all 0: plotly then spread the axis from -100% to +100% low = min(float(dd.min()), -0.01) * 1.05 fig.update_yaxes(tickformat=".0%", title="Drawdown", range=[low, -low * 0.04], row=2, col=1) if few_days: # one tick per day: plotly labelled the hours between two closes fig.update_xaxes(tickformat="%b %d", dtick=86_400_000) if intraday: # hide weekends and nights, but only for markets closed then (crypto never is) hours = hours or {"nights": False, "weekends": False} breaks = ([] if hours["weekends"] else [dict(bounds=["sat", "mon"])]) + \ ([] if hours["nights"] else [dict(bounds=[16, 9.5], pattern="hour")]) if breaks: fig.update_xaxes(rangebreaks=breaks) return fig PARTY_FILL = "rgba(128,128,128,0.18)" # neutral gray: blue and red already mean other things here def _shade_parties(fig, dates): """Shade the Democratic presidencies in gray (Republican ones stay clear), with the president's name above any term wide enough to label. Party colors are not used: on this site blue is the fundamentalists and red a loss.""" terms = ex.party_terms(dates) if not terms: return span = (dates[-1] - dates[0]).days or 1 for t in terms: wide = (t["end"] - t["start"]).days / span > 0.075 if t["party"] == "D": fig.add_vrect(x0=t["start"], x1=t["end"], fillcolor=PARTY_FILL, line_width=0, layer="below", row="all", col=1) if wide: # at the bottom of the price panel: at the top they ran into the legend fig.add_annotation(x=t["start"] + (t["end"] - t["start"]) / 2, y=0.01, yref="y domain", xref="x", text=f"{t['name']} ({t['party']})", showarrow=False, yanchor="bottom", textangle=-90 if (t["end"] - t["start"]).days / span < 0.12 else 0, font=dict(size=10, color=c.MUTED)) def _party_panel(name, r, mixes, run): """The president's-party numbers for the market on screen (explore.party_view), and the model's own gap on the same calendar: luck alone when the party drift is 0.""" v, why = c.party_view(r) st.markdown("**President's party**") if v is None: st.caption(f"{name}'s history can't be split by party: it {why}.") return luck = v["luck"] def verdict(pct): return f"unusual ({pct:.0f}%)" if pct < 5 or pct > 95 else f"about what luck gives ({pct:.0f}%)" c.stats_row([ ("Gap a year, D − R", f"{v['gap_year']:+.1%}", None, "Average yearly return under Democratic presidents " "minus under Republican ones (log returns, price only)."), ("Under Democrats", f"{v['dem_year']:+.1%} a year", None, None), ("Under Republicans", f"{v['rep_year']:+.1%} a year", None, None), ("Luck test", f"beats {luck['mean']:.0f}% of {v['calendars']}", None, "Fake calendars: the real presidents' terms slid along this market's own history (whole quarters, " "at least a year from the real dates). A gap that beats more than 95% of them would be unusual."), ("Volatility D ÷ R", f"{v['vol_ratio']:.2f}", None, "Daily ups and downs under Democrats divided by " "under Republicans (1 = the same)."), ("Crash days D − R", f"{v['crashes']:+.1f} per 1,000", None, "Days falling more than 4 standard " "deviations, per 1,000 days, under Democrats minus Republicans."), ]) herd = mixes["herding"][0] model_line = "" if herd is not None: g = ex.model_party_gap(herd) model_line = (f" The herding model on the same presidents' calendar gives {g:+.1%} a year" + (f", with your party drift of {run['party']:+.1f}%." if run.get("party", 0.0) else ": it has no politics, so that gap is pure luck.")) st.caption( f"{v['start']:%Y}–{v['end']:%Y}, {v['changes']} changes of party.     its value for max_days trading days in a row, or ever more than e^HARD_GAP
    (the paper: no *persistent* pathological mispricing). Bubbles that burst on
    their own are kept. max_gap=None switches every runaway check off: the price may
    then go anywhere (meant for tests that push the model to extremes on purpose).

    check(p)
    if isinstance(days, (bool, np.bool_)) or not isinstance(days, (int, np.integer)) or days < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"days must be a whole number >= 1, got {days!r}")
    if not isinstance(chartists, (bool, np.bool_)):
        raise ValueError(f"chartists must be True or False, got {chartists!r}")
    N, floor = int(p["N"]), int(p["floor"])
    each = max(int(N * START_CHARTISTS) // 2, floor) if chartists else 0
    if max_gap is not None and not (isinstance(max_gap, (int, float, np.number))
                                    and not isinstance(max_gap, (bool, np.bool_)) and max_gap > 0):
        raise ValueError(f"max_gap must be a number above 0, or None, got {max_gap!r}")
    if isinstance(max_days, (bool, np.bool_)) or not isinstance(max_days, (int, np.integer)) \
            or max_days < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"max_days must be a whole number >= 1, got {max_days!r}")
    check_breakers(breakers)
    check_shocks(shocks, days)
    if breakers is None:
        cb, halt_steps, pause_end = (-np.inf, -np.inf, -np.inf), 0, 0
    else:
        cb = tuple(float(np.log(1.0 - x)) for x in breakers["levels"])
        halt_steps = pause_steps(breakers["halt_minutes"], p["dt"])
        pause_end = minute_to_step(breakers.get("last_pause_minute", MINUTES_PER_DAY), p["dt"])
    shock = np.zeros(int(days))
    for day, frac in (shocks or {}).items():
        shock[day] += np.log1p(frac)
    lp, lf, z, x, halts, done, ran_away = _simulate(
        np.random.default_rng(seed), int(days), int(round(1 / p["dt"])), bool(chartists),
        N, *(float(p[k]) for k in ("v1", "v2", "a1", "a2", "a3", "s", "R", "tc", "gamma",
                                   "beta", "sigma_mu", "sigma_eps", "tick")),
        floor, each, each, np.inf if max_gap is None else float(max_gap), int(max_days),
        np.inf if max_gap is None else HARD_GAP, *cb, int(halt_steps), int(pause_end), shock)
    if ran_away:
        ratio = np.exp(min(abs(lp[done] - lf[done]), 700.0))   # 700: largest safe exponent
        raise RunawayError(f"day {done}: the price is {ratio:.3g}x away from its value with "
                           f"{z[done]:.0%} chartists and has not come back (a runaway "
                           f"{'bubble' if lp[done] > lf[done] else 'crash'})", done)
    return dict(r=np.diff(lp), lp=lp, lf=lf, z=z, x=x, halts=halts)

    """The first `day` + 1 daily closes (lp, lf, z) of a history that ran away on `day`,
    rebuilt by rerunning the same seed with the runaway guard off (max_gap=None). The
    guard only stops a run, it never changes its random draws, so the path is the same."""

GAP_CAP = 0.5            # the Story chart shows mispricing up to e^0.5 - 1 = +65%; beyond is "off the chart"


def runaway_story(p, seed, day, burn, mix="chartists", a1=0.0):
    """What the Story page tells about a history that ran away on `day` (counted after burn-in):
    z, the share of chartists each day; gap, how far the price sits above (+) or below (-) its
    value, as a fraction, capped at +-(e^GAP_CAP - 1); both from day 0 to `day` with the burn-in
    (warm-up) days left out, so day 0 here is day 0 in the text and the Workspace; gap_cap, that cap;
    share_before, the share of chartists 5 days before the end; calm_days, about how long the
    price stayed near its value (all but the last 3 days)."""
    day = _whole(day, "day", 1)
    burn = _whole(burn, "burn", 0)
    path = runaway_path(p, mix, a1, seed, day + burn)
    z = path["z"][burn:]
    gap = np.expm1(np.clip(path["lp"] - path["lf"], -GAP_CAP, GAP_CAP))[burn:]
    return {"z": z, "gap": gap, "gap_cap": float(np.expm1(GAP_CAP)),
            "share_before": float(z[max(len(z) - 6, 0)]),
            "calm_days": max(day - 3, 0)}       # a runaway on day 1-3 had no calm stretch (not -2 days)

def model_market(p, burn, mix, a1, a2, v1, days, seed, party=0.0):
    """The simulated market behind one trader mix, day by day after the burn-in, for the Test
    program's "Model market" chart: the same history as run_mixes gives for that mix (same seed,
    settings and party drift). Returns a dict of numpy arrays, one value per day's close:
        price   the price, as an index that starts at 100 on day 0
        value   the fundamental value on the same scale (the price it is pulled back to)
        z       share of traders who are chartists (0-1)
        x       chartists' mood, (optimists - pessimists) / chartists (-1 to 1)
        r       the daily log returns (one fewer value), exactly run_mixes' returns for this mix
    and runaway_day: None, or the day (after burn-in) the history ran away. A history that ran away
    is shown up to that day, rebuilt with the runaway guard off (it never changes the random draws,
    so those days are the same); one that ran away in the warm-up has nothing to show (ValueError)."""
    q, chartists = mix_settings(dict(p, a2=a2, v1=v1), mix, a1)
    days, burn = _whole(days, "days", 1), _whole(burn, "burn", 0)
    seed = _whole(seed, "seed", 0)
    shocks = party_shocks(days, burn, party)
    ran = None
    try:
        out = model.simulate(q, days + burn, seed=seed, chartists=chartists, shocks=shocks)
    except model.RunawayError as e:
        ran = runaway_day(e, burn)
        if ran < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"this history ran away in the warm-up, before day 0") from e
        out = model.simulate(q, int(e.day), seed=seed, chartists=chartists, max_gap=None,
                             shocks={d: f for d, f in (shocks or {}).items() if d < e.day})
    lp, lf = out["lp"][burn:], out["lf"][burn:]
    return {"price": 100 * np.exp(lp - lp[0]), "value": 100 * np.exp(lf - lp[0]),
            "z": out["z"][burn:], "x": out["x"][burn:], "r": np.diff(lp), "runaway_day": ran}

    moves by +party/2 a year (spread over the trading days) under a Democratic president and by

    5 points). The burn-in days get none. party = 0 gives None: the model exactly as in SPEC.md."""

def moves_in_sd(r, ref=None):
    """Each move of r in standard deviations of `ref` (default: r itself): (r - mean) / sd, with
    the population sd (ddof=0) like stats.standardize, so a "4 sd" day means the same on every
    chart. A Series keeps its dates."""
    x = stats._returns(r)
    base = x if ref is None else stats._returns(ref)
    if base.max() == base.min():
        raise ValueError("reference returns are constant: no spread to measure")
    sd = base.std()
    if not np.isfinite(sd) or sd <= 0:
        raise ValueError("reference returns are too large or too small to measure their spread")
    z = (x - base.mean()) / sd
    return pd.Series(z, index=r.index, name=r.name) if isinstance(r, pd.Series) else z

def big_day_list(r, size=BIG, within=None):
    """Days that moved more than `size` standard deviations: a DataFrame indexed like r with
    columns move (the simple return, e.g. -0.2 = -20%) and sd (the move in standard deviations),
    biggest first. r is a Series of daily log returns. sd is always measured against all of r;
    `within` (dates, or a Series whose dates are used) keeps only the big days among them, e.g.
    the range a chart shows. Rows are found by position, so a repeated date can't mix rows up."""
    r = pd.Series(r, dtype=float)
    z = moves_in_sd(r.values)
    pos = np.flatnonzero(np.abs(z) > size)
    pos = pos[np.argsort(-np.abs(z[pos]), kind="stable")]
    out = pd.DataFrame({"move": np.expm1(r.values[pos]), "sd": z[pos]}, index=r.index[pos])

    return out

  I fetched three pages: Nicky Case's Parable of the Polygons, Bret Victor's Explorable Explanations essay and Distill's t-SNE article. Evolution of Trust only returned its loading screen. For Google Finance I found news coverage but no current description of the quote page. So the Robinhood, Yahoo, TradingView and Google Finance points below come from my own knowledge of those pages, not from anything I checked today.
  
  Patterns, with how each fits your page:
  
  1. **One big number with a colored change line under it** (Robinhood, Google Finance). Lead with one answer, such as "Biggest crash: −22% in a day (real) vs −9% (simulated)", colored by direction. This replaces the 7-number stats row.
  2. **A sentence that updates with the result** (Bret Victor's reactive documents, Polygons). Put one plain sentence under the chart and rewrite it as the slider moves. Example: "At this herding strength, the model's crashes are about as fat-tailed as the S&P 500's."
  3. **Main control in the sentence or right beside the chart** (Victor's adjustable numbers in sentences, Polygons' bias slider placed next to its simulation). Keep only the herding-strength slider next to the chart. Move the other five sliders into a collapsed "Advanced model settings" section.
  4. **Real and simulated side by side on the same axes** (Distill's input-on-the-left, output-on-the-right layout and its small multiples). Use two matching panels, real and model, with the same scale so they can be compared at a glance. This is better than a "Price" vs "Model market" toggle.
  5. **A few range buttons tucked under the chart** (Robinhood, Google Finance). Cut the seven range buttons to three or four (1Y, 10Y, All) and set them small, below the chart.
  6. **Advanced views hidden until asked for** (TradingView keeps indicators behind a menu on an otherwise clean chart). Show the price view by default. Put Tail, Histogram, Bursts and Memory under a "Look closer" tab or expander, each with a one-line caption saying what to look for.
  7. **Term definitions on hover or an info icon** (Google Finance key stats, Victor's contextual information). Give "fat tails", "kurtosis" and "volatility clustering" an info icon with a one-sentence definition instead of a separate table.
  8. **Prompts that set a small task** (Polygons). Add three preset buttons: "No herding", "Some herding", "Strong herding". Each sets the slider and asks a question, e.g. "Do crashes appear?"
  9. **Introduce one idea at a time** (Polygons moves from one rule, to an auto-run, to a graph, to a free sandbox). Order the page: the real market first, then the model with no herding (calm and Gaussian), then the slider, then the advanced views. The free play area goes last.
  10. **A pass/fail summary instead of tables** (Polygons' running segregation graph gives one clear readout). Replace the dial chart and the three tables with a small three-row checklist of tails, crashes and clustering. Each row shows matches / close / doesn't match against the S&P 500.
  11. **Sensible defaults and a shareable view** (Distill sets defaults and has a "Share this view" link). Open the page at the best-fit herding setting so the first screen already makes the point. Keep the settings in the URL query string so a view can be linked.

input.description: Audit engine against spec and paper
input.prompt:
Project: /Users/avishjain/02-120 Project (student implementation of the Lux & Marchesi 1999 herding market model; read CLAUDE.md first). Goal: an independent read-only accuracy audit of the simulation engine, `herding/model.py` (function `_simulate` and `simulate`), against `docs/SPEC.md` and the published model.

Do:
1. Read docs/SPEC.md and herding/model.py carefully. For each equation in SPEC (transition rates between optimists/pessimists/fundamentalists, U1, U2,1, U2,2, excess demand, price change probability, fundamental value news, floors, trend window, dt scaling), check the code implements it exactly — signs, factors like v1·nc/N, v2·n_f/N, the a2/v1 trend term, R, s, the |gap| term, tick handling, the mu noise scaling with dt.
2. Compare SPEC against outside sources you can read on the public web: the Samanidou, Zschischang, Stauffer & Lux (2007) review "Agent-based models of financial markets" (Rep. Prog. Phys.; arXiv physics/0701140), Lux & Marchesi (2000) "Volatility clustering in financial markets: a microsimulation of interacting agents" (IJTAF) if available, and any other reputable description of the Lux–Marchesi model. Note the parameter values the literature uses (N=500, v1, v2, beta, Tc, Tf/gamma, a1,a2,a3, R, r, s, sigma_mu, sigma_eps, dt) and compare to `settings/paper_matched.json` and model.py defaults.
3. Optionally run small numeric checks (python3 from the project folder), e.g. that with chartists=False returns are Gaussian (excess kurtosis ≈ 0) and that results with numba (default) and with env MODEL_NO_NUMBA=1 agree exactly on a short run (e.g. 200 days, seed 1). Keep any scratch files in `scratch/` inside the project, never /tmp.

Do NOT edit any project files (other work is editing herding/explore.py, web/ and tests right now). Report under 450 words: each discrepancy found (file:line, what the code does, what the spec/literature says, how much it matters), anything confirmed correct, and the sources you actually read (with URLs). """Tests of the November 2026 additions behind the Test program page (herding/explore.py):
run_mixes running its three mixes at the same time, model_market (the "Simulated market" chart),
the fresh end of live prices (recent_prices, splice_recent), Yahoo's live quote (live_quote) and
the model-vs-market scorecard. No test uses the internet: Yahoo is always a fake here."""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pytest

from herding import explore as ex
from herding import model

P, BURN = ex.fitted_settings()
A1, A2, V1 = float(P["a1"]), float(P["a2"]), float(P["v1"])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ run_mixes in parallel

# Spec: the same histories as running each mix alone, one after another (the threads share nothing).
def test_parallel_run_mixes_equals_one_mix_at_a_time():
    out = ex.run_mixes(P, BURN, A1, 0.3, 1.5, 3000, 11, party=0.02)
    q = dict(P, a2=0.3, v1=1.5)
    for m in ex.MIXES:
        r, err = ex.run_mix(q, m, A1, 3000, 11, BURN, 0.02)
        assert (out[m][0] is None) == (r is None)
        if r is not None:
            assert np.array_equal(out[m][0], r)
        else:
            assert out[m][1] == ex.runaway_day(err, BURN)


# Spec: a bad input still raises the same ValueError (it is raised inside a thread, then passed on).
def test_parallel_run_mixes_passes_errors_on():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="days"):
        ex.run_mixes(P, BURN, A1, A2, V1, 10, 0)


# Spec: running it twice gives the same numbers (no shared random state between the threads).
def test_parallel_run_mixes_is_repeatable():
    a = ex.run_mixes(P, BURN, A1, A2, V1, 2000, 5)
    b = ex.run_mixes(P, BURN, A1, A2, V1, 2000, 5)
    for m in ex.MIXES:
        assert (a[m][0] is None and b[m][0] is None) or np.array_equal(a[m][0], b[m][0])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ model_market

# Spec: its returns are exactly run_mixes' returns for that mix, and price/value start where they should.
@pytest.mark.parametrize("party", [0.0, 0.03])
def test_model_market_is_the_same_history_as_run_mixes(party):
    mixes = ex.run_mixes(P, BURN, A1, A2, V1, 3000, 3, party=party)
    for m in ex.MIXES:
        if mixes[m][0] is None:
            continue
        mm = ex.model_market(P, BURN, m, A1, A2, V1, 3000, 3, party)
        assert mm["runaway_day"] is None
        assert np.array_equal(mm["r"], mixes[m][0])
        assert len(mm["price"]) == len(mm["value"]) == len(mm["z"]) == len(mm["x"]) == 3001
        assert mm["price"][0] == 100.0
        # the price index follows the returns: 100 * exp(cumulative log return)
        assert np.allclose(mm["price"][1:], 100 * np.exp(np.cumsum(mm["r"])), rtol=1e-12)


# Spec: fundamentalists only have no chartists (share 0) and their price stays near the value.
def test_model_market_fundamentalists_have_no_chartists():
    mm = ex.model_market(P, BURN, "fundamentalists", A1, A2, V1, 2000, 1)
    assert np.all(mm["z"] == 0)
    assert np.max(np.abs(np.log(mm["price"] / mm["value"]))) < 0.2


# Spec: chartist share is a fraction and mood is between -1 and 1.
def test_model_market_shares_are_in_range():
    mm = ex.model_market(P, BURN, "herding", A1, A2, V1, 2000, 2)
    assert np.all((mm["z"] >= 0) & (mm["z"] <= 1))
    assert np.all((mm["x"] >= -1) & (mm["x"] <= 1))


# Spec: a history that runs away is shown up to its runaway day, and that day matches run_mixes.
def test_model_market_runaway_stops_on_the_runaway_day():
    mixes = ex.run_mixes(P, BURN, 0.0, A2, V1, 10000, 0)
    day = mixes["chartists"][1]
    assert day is not None and day > 0               # documented: chartists, seed 0 run away
    mm = ex.model_market(P, BURN, "chartists", 0.0, A2, V1, 10000, 0)
    assert mm["runaway_day"] == day
    assert len(mm["price"]) == day + 1
    # the days before are the same draws as the full run would have made
    q, _ = ex.mix_settings(P, "chartists", 0.0)
    full = model.simulate(q, BURN + day, seed=0, max_gap=None)
    assert np.array_equal(mm["r"], np.diff(full["lp"][BURN:]))


# Spec: a history that ran away in the warm-up has nothing to show: ValueError.
def test_model_market_warmup_runaway_raises():
    mixes = ex.run_mixes(P, BURN, 0.0, 1.0, 5.0, 5000, 1)
    assert mixes["chartists"][1] is not None and mixes["chartists"][1] < 1   # documented case
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="warm-up"):
        ex.model_market(P, BURN, "chartists", 0.0, 1.0, 5.0, 5000, 1)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [dict(mix="traders"), dict(a1=-1.0), dict(seed=-1), dict(days=0)])
def test_model_market_rejects_bad_input(bad):
    kw = dict(mix="herding", a1=A1, a2=A2, v1=V1, days=1000, seed=0)
    kw.update(bad)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        ex.model_market(P, BURN, kw["mix"], kw["a1"], kw["a2"], kw["v1"], kw["days"], kw["seed"])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ recent_prices / splice_recent

def _closes(dates, values, name="T"):
    return pd.Series(values, index=pd.DatetimeIndex(dates), name=name, dtype=float)


# Spec: asks Yahoo from RECENT_DAYS calendar days before today, and keeps only those dates.
def test_recent_prices_asks_for_the_last_days_only():
    asked = []

    def fake(t, start):
        asked.append((t, start))
        return _closes(["2026-11-01", "2026-11-20", "2026-11-23", "2026-11-24"], [1, 2, 3, 4])
    out = ex.recent_prices("abc", download=fake, today="2026-11-24 15:00")
    assert asked == [("ABC", "2026-11-14")]
    assert list(out.values) == [2, 3, 4] and out.name == "ABC"


# Spec: a bar stamped within the day becomes its date (the last one of a day wins); a time zone is
# dropped without moving the date (BE-18).
def test_recent_prices_dates_and_time_zones():
    idx = pd.DatetimeIndex(["2026-11-23 00:00", "2026-11-24 00:00"]).tz_localize("UTC")
    out = ex.recent_prices("BTC-USD", download=lambda t, s: pd.Series([5.0, 6.0], index=idx),
                           today="2026-11-24")
    assert list(out.index.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")) == ["2026-11-23", "2026-11-24"]


def test_recent_prices_errors():
    with pytest.raises(ConnectionError):
        ex.recent_prices("ABC", download=lambda t, s: 1 / 0, today="2026-11-24")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="no recent prices"):
        ex.recent_prices("ABC", download=lambda t, s: pd.Series(dtype=float), today="2026-11-24")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        ex.recent_prices("not a ticker!", download=lambda t, s: None)


# Spec: newer closes replace the same dates and later dates are added, in order.
def test_splice_recent_updates_and_appends():
    close = _closes(["2026-11-18", "2026-11-19", "2026-11-20"], [10, 11, 12], "S")
    recent = _closes(["2026-11-19", "2026-11-20", "2026-11-23"], [11, 12.5, 13])
    out = ex.splice_recent(close, recent)
    assert list(out.values) == [10, 11, 12.5, 13] and out.name == "S"
    assert out.index.is_monotonic_increasing and not out.index.has_duplicates


# Spec: recent prices that start after the history's last close are not added (the days between
# would be missing); None or empty recent leaves the history as it is.
def test_splice_recent_never_leaves_a_gap():
    close = _closes(["2026-10-29", "2026-10-30"], [10, 11])
    later = _closes(["2026-11-20", "2026-11-23"], [20, 21])
    assert ex.splice_recent(close, later).equals(close)
    assert ex.splice_recent(close, None).equals(close)
    assert ex.splice_recent(close, _closes([], [])).equals(close)


# Spec: dates in recent older than RECENT_DAYS before the history's end can't rewrite old data.
def test_splice_recent_keeps_old_data():
    close = _closes(pd.bdate_range("2026-10-01", "2026-10-30"), np.arange(22.0))
    recent = _closes(["2026-10-02", "2026-10-30"], [999, 50])
    out = ex.splice_recent(close, recent)
    assert out["2026-10-02"] == close["2026-10-02"] and out["2026-10-30"] == 50


def test_splice_recent_needs_dates():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        ex.splice_recent(pd.Series([1.0, 2.0]), None)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ live_quote

def test_live_quote_change():
    q = ex.live_quote("spy", quote=lambda t: (110.0, 100.0))
    assert q == {"price": 110.0, "prev_close": 100.0, "change": pytest.approx(0.1, abs=1e-12)}


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [(None, 100.0), (0.0, 100.0), (-1.0, 100.0), (np.nan, 100.0),
                                 (100.0, np.inf), (100.0, 0.0), ("x", 1.0)])
def test_live_quote_rejects_nonsense(bad):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        ex.live_quote("SPY", quote=lambda t: bad)


def test_live_quote_network_trouble_is_a_connection_error():
    with pytest.raises(ConnectionError):
        ex.live_quote("SPY", quote=lambda t: 1 / 0)


# Spec: the tests never reach the internet: conftest makes the real quote act as if Yahoo were down.
def test_tests_have_no_live_quotes():
    with pytest.raises(ConnectionError):
        ex.live_quote("SPY")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ scorecard

def _summ(tail, big, days, memory):
    return {"tail": tail, "big_days": big, "days": days, "memory": memory}


def test_scorecard_verdicts():
    market = _summ(3.0, 10, 10000, 0.20)
    same = ex.scorecard(market, _summ(3.0, 10, 10000, 0.20))
    assert [r["verdict"] for r in same] == ["match"] * 3
    assert [r["what"] for r in same] == ["Fat tails", "Crash days", "Wild days bunch up"]
    close = ex.scorecard(market, _summ(3.6, 20, 10000, 0.29))       # 20% off, 2x, 0.09 apart
    assert [r["verdict"] for r in close] == ["close"] * 3
    off = ex.scorecard(market, _summ(6.0, 0, 10000, 0.0))
    assert [r["verdict"] for r in off] == ["off"] * 3


# Spec: crash days are compared per 1,000 days, so histories of different lengths compare fairly.
def test_scorecard_crash_days_per_1000():
    rows = ex.scorecard(_summ(3.0, 10, 10000, 0.2), _summ(3.0, 20, 20000, 0.2))
    assert rows[1]["market"] == rows[1]["model"] == 1.0 and rows[1]["verdict"] == "match"


# Spec: the edges of each rule: exactly on the match limit is a match.
def test_scorecard_edges():
    m = _summ(3.0, 10, 10000, 0.2)
    assert ex.scorecard(m, _summ(3.3, 15, 10000, 0.25))[0]["verdict"] == "match"
    assert ex.scorecard(m, _summ(3.0, 15, 10000, 0.2))[1]["verdict"] == "match"
    assert ex.scorecard(m, _summ(3.0, 0, 10000, 0.2))[1]["verdict"] == "off"
    assert ex.scorecard(_summ(3.0, 0, 10000, 0.2), _summ(3.0, 0, 5000, 0.2))[1]["verdict"] == "match"


def test_scorecard_ran_away():
    assert ex.scorecard(_summ(3.0, 10, 10000, 0.2), None) == []

  I found no bugs. Every equation in SPEC is implemented exactly in `_simulate`, with the right signs and factors. The only gaps with the literature are deliberate choices that SPEC already documents. One of them, the tick-rate units, is large. No project files were edited.
  
  ### Checked line by line, all correct
  - **Mood rates (lines 220-225):** `v1*nc/N*exp(±U1)`, with pessimist→optimist using `exp(+U1)`. U1 at line 216 is `a1*x + a2/v1*trend`. Matches [S] eq 17.
  - **Strategy switches (lines 217-219, 222-227):** a fundamentalist joining a mood group has rate `v2*n±/N*exp(U2,±)`; leaving it has `v2*n_f/N*exp(-U2,±)`. `gain = R(1+gap) + trend/v2` is the same as (r + ṗ/v2)/p, because r = R·p_f and 1+gap = p_f/p. U2,1 and U2,2 have the right signs, with the `s*|gap|` term. Matches [S] eqs 18-21.
  - **Excess demand (line 247):** `(n+ - n-)tc + n_f·γ·(p_f-p)/p`. Matches [S] eqs 22-23.
  - **Trend (line 209):** price change over 10 steps of 0.01, divided by the price at the start of the window, as SPEC says.
  - **Price noise mu and news (lines 186-187, 275):** both scale with dt as SPEC says.
  - **Floors (lines 229-242):** neither loop can drive a count negative or leave a group below the floor, given N ≥ 4·floor. Each trader moves at most once per step (`_leave`).
  - **Order within a step:** switch, then tick, then news. Matches SPEC.

  - With numba and with `MODEL_NO_NUMBA=1`, the paper-matched settings for 200 days on seed 1 give **identical** lp, lf, z and x (largest difference 0.0).
  - With no chartists, excess kurtosis over 5 seeds of 20,000 days is 0.006 to 0.047, which is about zero (the expected noise is roughly ±0.035).

  1. **Tick-rate units (line 251, `/tick`): large.** [S] says the auctioneer moves the price "by one elementary unit (one cent...)" with probability w per Δt. Zawadowski et al. say the market maker may "increase the price by 0.01 with the probability π↑p". So in the original, β(ED+μ) is a rate of one-cent ticks, and the code's rate is 1/tick = 1000 times higher. The code follows [S] eq 25, which says (dp/dt)/p = β·ED. The consequence is that β, tc, γ and σ_mu cannot be compared with the published values.   ## Audit of `herding/model.py` against SPEC and the literature
  
  I found no bugs. Every equation in SPEC is implemented exactly in `_simulate`, with the right signs and factors. The only gaps with the literature are deliberate choices that SPEC already documents. One of them, the tick-rate units, is large. No project files were edited.
  
  ### Checked line by line, all correct
  - **Mood rates (lines 220-225):** `v1*nc/N*exp(±U1)`, with pessimist→optimist using `exp(+U1)`. U1 at line 216 is `a1*x + a2/v1*trend`. Matches [S] eq 17.
  - **Strategy switches (lines 217-219, 222-227):** a fundamentalist joining a mood group has rate `v2*n±/N*exp(U2,±)`; leaving it has `v2*n_f/N*exp(-U2,±)`. `gain = R(1+gap) + trend/v2` is the same as (r + ṗ/v2)/p, because r = R·p_f and 1+gap = p_f/p. U2,1 and U2,2 have the right signs, with the `s*|gap|` term. Matches [S] eqs 18-21.
  - **Excess demand (line 247):** `(n+ - n-)tc + n_f·γ·(p_f-p)/p`. Matches [S] eqs 22-23.
  - **Trend (line 209):** price change over 10 steps of 0.01, divided by the price at the start of the window, as SPEC says.
  - **Price noise mu and news (lines 186-187, 275):** both scale with dt as SPEC says.
  - **Floors (lines 229-242):** neither loop can drive a count negative or leave a group below the floor, given N ≥ 4·floor. Each trader moves at most once per step (`_leave`).
  - **Order within a step:** switch, then tick, then news. Matches SPEC.
  
  ### Numeric checks (scripts and outputs in `scratch/`)
  - With numba and with `MODEL_NO_NUMBA=1`, the paper-matched settings for 200 days on seed 1 give **identical** lp, lf, z and x (largest difference 0.0).
  - With no chartists, excess kurtosis over 5 seeds of 20,000 days is 0.006 to 0.047, which is about zero (the expected noise is roughly ±0.035).
  
  ### Differences from the literature (all documented in SPEC)
  1. **Tick-rate units (line 251, `/tick`): large.** [S] says the auctioneer moves the price "by one elementary unit (one cent...)" with probability w per Δt. Zawadowski et al. say the market maker may "increase the price by 0.01 with the probability π↑p". So in the original, β(ED+μ) is a rate of one-cent ticks, and the code's rate is 1/tick = 1000 times higher. The code follows [S] eq 25, which says (dp/dt)/p = β·ED. The consequence is that β, tc, γ and σ_mu cannot be compared with the published values. The code's `SET_I` gives a 4.0% daily sd and excess kurtosis 11.8 over 2000 days, so it is not the published set I. The fitted settings absorb this.

content.text:
The Test program page now updates on its own when you move a slider, shows the simulated market day by day, and gets live Yahoo prices. All 1,457 tests and the project's web stress test pass. Nothing is committed yet.

**Speed**
- One model run now takes about 0.4 s instead of 0.8 s. The three trader mixes (fundamentalists only, chartists who don't herd, chartists who herd) used to run one after another; now they run at the same time on different processor cores.
- The numbers are exactly the same as before. I checked this against running each mix alone.

**Live prices**
- Before, a "live" price could be up to a day old, because Yahoo's data was saved for 24 hours.
- Now the header asks Yahoo for the latest price every 15 seconds. The chart's most recent days update every minute, and the long history is fetched once a day.
- I watched it update on its own in the browser (16:12:51, then 16:13:52; the hidden browser pane slows the timer). Today's S&P 500 showed 7,201.09.

**Page layout**

I had a subagent look at clean designs online (Nicky Case's *Parable of the Polygons*, Bret Victor's interactive essays, finance quote pages) and used the ideas that fit:
- **One main control:** the herding-strength slider stays in view; the other five settings are under "More model settings".
- **Auto-run:** moving a slider runs the model straight away. A "Run automatically" switch turns this off.
- **Scorecard:** "How close is the model to the S&P 500?" checks three things against the real market, each marked ✓ (as close as luck allows), ≈ or ✗:
  - fat tails: how often very big days happen
  - crash days: days that moved more than 4 standard deviations
  - wild days bunching together

  At the default setting all three match.
- **Plain view names:** for example, "How rare big days are" instead of "Tail".
- **New "Simulated market" chart:** three panels.
  - the model's price next to its true value (the price traders think the stock is really worth)
  - the share of traders who are chartists (traders who follow trends and copy the crowd)
  - optimists minus pessimists as a share of all traders, which is what pushes the price in the model

  In that last panel, the spikes line up with the clusters of crash days.

**Accuracy (checked by subagents)**
- **Engine:** read line by line against `docs/SPEC.md` and two published sources: Samanidou et al. 2007 and Zawadowski et al. 2002. No bugs found. With no chartists, returns come out bell-shaped, as the proposal requires: excess kurtosis 0.006–0.047 (it should be about 0).
- **S&P 500 data:** matches FRED (the Federal Reserve's public data site) on 2,495 of 2,496 days. The one difference is 0.12%, on 2021-08-11.
- **Dow data:** 17 closes were wrong. Most were typing slips; 25 Sep 2002 reads 7,481.82 instead of 7,841.82, which created a fake +6.7% day. I added them to the list of known bad closes the program skips. The effect on the Dow's statistics is small: tail exponent 2.736 → 2.735, 252 → 251 big days. `python3 scripts/analysis/data_crosscheck.py` reruns this check.

**Dead code:** removed two functions nothing used (`spx_target`, `past_year`) and a few unused imports.

**Left for you:**
- `figures/RESULTS.md` still says the Dow has 35,247 days (now 35,230), and its president's-party numbers were computed before the Dow fix. Rerun `python3 scripts/party_figures.py` to update them.
- The saved Dow file is missing 8 trading days from 2026. Downloading the data again would fill them in.
- The engine review found that the model's price-step size uses different units from the original paper. This is a choice SPEC already documents, but it means our fitted settings can't be compared directly with the paper's numbers. Also, no source was found for the size of the daily news noise (σ_ε = 0.005).

When you're ready to commit, send me a message in your own words, since CLAUDE.md asks for that.

To try it: `streamlit run app.py`, then open Test program. Click "Simulated market", drag the herding slider, and watch the scorecard change.

  **Setup:** Streamlit 1.67.0 and Plotly 7.1.0 are installed. None of the extra packages are (plotly-resampler, the lightweight-charts wrappers, streamlit-extras, st-aggrid, streamlit-echarts, streamlit-autorefresh). requirements.txt asks for `streamlit>=1.50` and `plotly>=6.0`. Release dates and licences come from the PyPI JSON API, checked today. I installed nothing and edited nothing.
  
  **Ranked recommendations (all built into Streamlit, no new dependencies):**
  
  1. **Selection events on the Plotly chart** (`st.plotly_chart(..., on_select="rerun", selection_mode=("points","box"))`). The page doesn't use this yet. Clicking a big-day marker could show that day's cause from `big_days_events.csv`. Box-selecting a stretch of history could fill the scorecard for just that window, for example 2008. Effort: about half a day. No new JavaScript, and the theme is unchanged.
  2. **Shareable links with `st.query_params`.** Write the ticker, range, slider values and seed into the URL, and read them back on load. Then a link reproduces an exact crash scenario. Effort: about 2 hours. One risk: writing to the URL inside a fragment can trigger extra reruns, so write it once per model run.
  3. **`st.dialog` and `st.status`.** A dialog could hold a "what is this number?" explainer for each scorecard figure without lengthening the page. `st.status` could cover the live-ticker download from Yahoo. Effort: about 1 hour each.
  4. **Optional: streamlit-echarts 0.7.0** (2026-06-08, MIT, needs Streamlit 1.53 or newer). Its built-in dataZoom slider zooms smoothly over 100 years of daily data. The cost is rewriting the charts and redoing the light/dark colours in a second chart style. Only worth it if Plotly feels slow on the "All" range.
  
  **Avoid:**
  - **plotly-resampler 0.11.1** (2026-10-04, MIT). Its requirements say `plotly<7.0.0`, so it conflicts with your Plotly 7.1. Re-sampling on zoom also needs Dash or FigureWidget callbacks, which Streamlit doesn't provide; the forum workaround embeds a separate Dash app in an iframe ([forum](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/could-i-make-streamlit-support-plotly-resampler/33089), [releases](https://github.com/predict-idlab/plotly-resampler/releases)). Downsampling the "All" range in your own code before plotting is simpler.
  - **streamlit-lightweight-charts 0.7.20** (last release 2023-05-22, unmaintained). The `-pro` fork's last release was 0.3.0 on 2025-12-06, from one author. It would also replace Plotly, dropping your drawdown panel and theme colours.
  - **streamlit-plotly-events** (last release 2021) and **streamlit-autorefresh** (2023). Built-in `on_select` and `st.fragment(run_every=...)` already do their jobs.
  - **st-aggrid 1.2.1.post2** (2025-12-29, MIT, a 2.0 release candidate is out). It adds a heavy JavaScript bundle, its look doesn't follow the theme, and `st.dataframe` with `column_config` is enough for your tables.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ big days with a known cause

DAY_EVENTS = market_data.DATA / "big_days_events.csv"


def day_events(path=DAY_EVENTS):
    """The Dow's 20 biggest days with their documented causes (data/big_days_events.csv): a DataFrame
    indexed by date with columns move_percent, event, kind and sources (a list of URLs)."""
    df = pd.read_csv(path, parse_dates=["date"]).set_index("date").sort_index()
    df["sources"] = [[u.strip() for u in str(s).split("|") if u.strip()] for s in df.pop("source_url")]
    return df


def day_story(day, move, sd, events=None):
    """What the page says about one big day a visitor clicked: the move, and the documented cause
    when that day is one of the Dow's 20 biggest (events: day_events()). Returns (text, sources)."""
    day = pd.Timestamp(day).normalize()
    text = (f"{day:%d %B %Y}: {'rose' if move > 0 else 'fell'} {abs(move):.1%}, "
            f"{abs(sd):.1f} standard deviations.")
    events = day_events() if events is None else events
    if day in events.index:
        e = events.loc[day]
        return text + f" What happened: {e['event']}", list(e["sources"])
    return text + " This day is not among the Dow's 20 biggest days, whose causes the project documents.", []


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ shareable links

LINK_LIMITS = {"a1": (0.0, 2.0), "a2": (0.0, 1.0), "v1": (0.5, 5.0), "party": (-10.0, 10.0)}
LINK_SEEDS = (0, 10_000)
LINK_KEYS = ("market", "a1", "a2", "v1", "party", "days", "seed")

The probe script is at /Users/avishjain/02-120 Project/scratch/apis/probe.py. No project code was changed.

| Endpoint | Result | Latency |
|---|---|---|
| FRED `fredgraph.csv?id=SP500` | Real CSV, 2,608 rows, last row 2026-11-23 = 7237.17. History starts only at **2016-11-25** (S&P licensing caps it at 10 years). | 0.05 s |
| FRED with a browser User-Agent (`Mozilla/5.0`) | **Blocked**: Akamai drops the connection or it times out after 30 s. Python's default UA and `python-requests` work. | — |
| FRED multi-series `id=DGS10,DCOILBRENTEU` | Real CSV | 5.4 s |
| FRED API without a key | HTTP 400, "api_key is not set" | 0.8 s |
| Stooq `q/d/l/?s=^spx` | **Block page**: HTTP 200, but the body is a 796-byte JavaScript proof-of-work challenge, not CSV. Same for `aapl.us`. | 0.3 s |
| CoinGecko simple price, no key | Real data, `{"bitcoin":{"usd":59867}}` | 0.09 s |
| CoinGecko 365-day chart, no key | Real data | 0.14 s |
| Yahoo raw `v8/finance/chart/^GSPC` (daily and 5-minute bars) | Real data | 0.14 s |
| Cboe `VIX_History.csv` | Real CSV, 1990-01-02 to 2026-11-23 | 0.2 s |
| `api.nasdaq.com` | Unofficial. An AAPL quote works (3.2 s), but SPX returns "Symbol not exists". | — |

Python's built-in `urllib` failed SSL checks on this machine until I passed `certifi`'s certificate bundle. `requests` and `yfinance` already do that.

## Ranked options

| # | Source | Key? | Free limits | Coverage | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **FRED** (fredgraph.csv) | No (the API needs a free key, about 120 requests/min) | Generous | S&P 500 and Dow daily closes, last 10 years only; rates, oil, dollar; no intraday | Best no-key fallback for daily closes. Use a plain Python User-Agent. |
| 2 | **Alpaca** market data | Yes (free account) | 200 calls/min; websocket up to 30 symbols | US stocks and ETFs since 2016; real-time IEX only (the full feed is 15 min delayed); no indexes (use SPY) | Best free real-time and intraday option, including streaming. |
| 3 | **Tiingo** | Yes | 50/hour, 1,000/day, 1 GB/month | Stocks and ETFs with decades of end-of-day history; IEX intraday | Clean end-of-day history, but the free plan is "internal use only" (displaying it publicly needs a paid license). |
| 4 | **Massive (formerly Polygon)** | Yes | 5 calls/min; end-of-day only; stocks 2 years, indexes about 1 year | Stocks and some index tickers | Fine as a light end-of-day backup, too limited for history. |
| 5 | **Twelve Data** / **Finnhub** | Yes | Twelve Data: 8/min, 800/day. Finnhub: 60/min, websocket for 50 symbols (reported) | Finnhub free has quotes but reportedly no historical candles; Twelve Data indexes need a paid plan | Usable for live quotes only. |
| 6 | **CoinGecko** | No (about 5/min shared per IP); free Demo key gives 100/min, 10k/month | Crypto only; attribution required | Works now; add it only if the app shows crypto. |

**Not worth it:**
- **Alpha Vantage**: 25 requests/day.
- **Financial Modeling Prep**: 250/day, 5-year history, index coverage unconfirmed.
- **Stooq**: blocked by the JavaScript challenge.
- **Nasdaq Data Link**: its free equity datasets have ended.
- **IEX Cloud**: shut down.

No free source goes back to 1950 for `^GSPC` except Yahoo. The saved files in `data/` remain the long-history source.

## Suggested plan

1. Keep `yfinance`.
2. On a Yahoo failure, fall back to FRED `SP500`/`DJIA` for daily closes, with the "10 years only" caveat shown.
3. Optionally, read Alpaca keys from Streamlit secrets for intraday data and quotes on SPY and stocks.
4. Cboe's VIX CSV is a free, no-key bonus.

FRED's behavior from Streamlit Cloud's IP addresses is untested.

- [FRED API errors / rate limits](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/errors.html)
- [Alpaca market data docs](https://docs.alpaca.markets/docs/about-market-data-api)
- [Tiingo documentation](https://api.tiingo.com/documentation)
- [Tiingo IEX API](https://api.tiingo.com/products/iex-api)
- [Massive indices](https://massive.com/indices)
- [Twelve Data pricing](https://twelvedata.com/pricing)
- [Finnhub pricing](https://finnhub.io/pricing)
- [Alpha Vantage premium](https://www.alphavantage.co/premium)
- [FMP pricing](https://site.financialmodelingprep.com/api/pricing-md)
- [CoinGecko keyless API](https://docs.coingecko.com/docs/keyless-public-api)
- [CoinGecko pricing](https://coingecko.com/api/pricing)

def style(fig, height=380, logx=False, logy=False, xtitle="", ytitle="", legend=True, hover="x unified",
          plain_log=False):
    """Chart in the visitor's mode, with the legend in its own strip above the plot so it never
    covers a line. hover:
      "x unified" (default, for lines over time that share their dates): one box reads every line
                  at the mouse's date, with a dotted crosshair, so the numbers follow the mouse;
      "closest"   for lines that don't share x values (the log-log tail curves, the herding dial)
                  and scatter maps: the box shows the one line or point under the mouse, no crosshair;
      "y unified" for horizontal bars.
    plain_log: label a log axis at powers of ten in plain numbers (1, 10, 100, 1,000) instead of
    plotly's 1k / 100μ (see log_ticks)."""
    p = pal()
    spikes = hover in ("x unified", "y unified")       # a crosshair only where one box reads every line
    fig.update_layout(template=p["TEMPLATE"], height=height, margin=dict(l=8, r=8, t=44 if legend else 12, b=8),
                      paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor=p["CARD"], hovermode=hover,
                      hoverdistance=-1, spikedistance=-1,
                      showlegend=legend, font=dict(size=12, family=MONO, color=p["TEXT2"]),
                      dragmode="zoom", uirevision="keep",
                      # namelength -1: the whole line name in the hover box, never cut to "Chartists wh..."
                      hoverlabel=dict(font=dict(family=MONO, size=12), bgcolor=p["PANEL"], bordercolor=p["LINE"],
                                      namelength=-1),
                      legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.01, xanchor="left", x=0,
                                  font=dict(size=12), bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)"))
    # "-" lets plotly choose (dates or numbers); forcing "linear" left the date axis empty
    axis = dict(showspikes=spikes, spikemode="across", spikesnap="cursor", spikethickness=1, spikedash="dot",
                spikecolor=p["MUTED"], gridcolor=p["GRID"], zeroline=False, linecolor=p["LINE"],
                tickfont=dict(size=12, color=p["MUTED"]), title_font=dict(size=12, color=p["MUTED"]))

    return fig
